About PhoenixAI

PhoenixAI is the Agentic AI Database, purpose-built to give autonomous AI agents sub-second access to live enterprise data at massive scale. The platform unifies real-time and at-rest data in a single AI-native engine, combining the speed and concurrency that agentic workloads demand with the governance and deployment flexibility enterprises require to put AI into production. Formerly known as CelerData, PhoenixAI is headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Learn more at phoenixdata.ai

About the role

We are seeking a talented Presales Solutions Architect to join our team and play a pivotal role in the sales cycle for our Agentic Database. You’ll partner with our sales team to guide prospects through the technical evaluation of PhoenixAI, delivering compelling presentations or demos, architecting tailored AI-native solutions, and securing technical wins. This customer-facing role requires a blend of deep technical expertise, strong communication skills, and a passion for solving complex data challenges.

What you'll do

As a Presales Solutions Architect, you’ll partner with sales to secure technical wins by showcasing PhoenixAI’s Agentic Database value and driving successful evaluations. Your responsibilities include:

• Technical Advocacy: Act as a trusted advisor, demonstrating PhoenixAI’s capabilities—like its vectorized query engine, lakehouse analytics, and multi-table joins for agentic AI workloads—via presentations, customized demos, and Proof of Concept (PoC).

• Solution Design: Work with prospects to understand their needs (e.g., data scale, latency, integrations) and architect PhoenixAI-based solutions to meet their goals.

• PoC Execution: Lead the design, implementation, and optimization of PoCs, ensuring prospects experience PhoenixAI’s Agentic Database performance and usability firsthand.

• Documentation: Keep detailed records of evaluations—covering use cases, challenges, PoC plans, and outcomes—to refine our process and inform product enhancements to PhoenixAI’s Agentic Database.

• Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with sales to align technical discussions with business goals, address objections, and close deals, while gathering customer insights to shape PhoenixAI’s Agentic Database roadmap with product and engineering teams.

• Marketing Support & Thought Leadership: Boost PhoenixAI’s presence by delivering webinars, staffing conference booths, speaking at user groups, and writing blogs on Agentic AI use cases and best practices.

Qualifications

• Ambition & Curiosity: A driven, inquisitive mindset—eager to learn PhoenixAI Agentic Database product’s intricacies, tackle tough challenges, and grow into the role, even if starting with less experience or specific skills.

• Experience: 3+ years in a pre-sales, solutions engineering, or technical consulting role, ideally within the data analytics, database, or cloud infrastructure space.

• Technical Expertise:

•

• Hands-on experience of OLAP workloads, query optimization, and data modeling (e.g., star schema, snowflake schema)

• Proficiency in SQL.

• Deep understanding of distributed data processing system theory.

• Familiar with at least one of the public cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure)

• Communication Skills: Proven ability to distill complex technical concepts into clear, compelling narratives for diverse stakeholders, from engineers to C-level executives.

• Problem-Solving: Adept at troubleshooting technical challenges during PoCs and adapting solutions to meet unique customer needs.

• Sales Mindset: Experience supporting sales teams in technical evaluations, with a track record of securing technical wins and driving revenue growth.

• Bonus Points:

•

• Knowledge of BI tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker)

• Experience with streaming processing systems (Kafka, Redpanda, etc.)

The base salary for this role is projected at $150,000-$200,000 annually, plus eligibility for PhoenixAI's bonus and equity programs.

Individual compensation will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location. We also provide a comprehensive benefits package featuring premium medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan. Employees enjoy at least 16 days of PTO, parental leave, health savings options, and access to our employee assistance program.

About the role

PhoenixAI is looking for an experienced Field Marketing Manager to own our in-person event programs end-to-end. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who has already managed high-stakes events at a tech startup — ideally in the data, infrastructure, or SaaS space — and understands how to allocate resources, manage vendors, and drive measurable outcomes.

Events are a key growth channel for PhoenixAI. The current program includes a monthly technical meetup (in the Bay Area and other U.S. cities), quarterly executive receptions for key customers, and a presence at major industry conferences such as AWS re:Invent. Our events motion is anchored in the StarRocks open-source community, and this role works closely with DevRel and Community to turn that community into a recurring, high-quality in-person program. This person will define clear goals for each program, execute flawlessly, and report results back to the business.

What you'll do

The Field Marketing Manager will own the full lifecycle of PhoenixAI's in-person events — strategy, budget, execution, and reporting — working cross-functionally to bring the right people and content into each program.

• Take full ownership of meetups, conferences, customer receptions, and partner programs from concept to close-out.

• Build and run a monthly technical meetup program in the Bay Area and other cities, drawing speakers and co-hosts from the StarRocks community, customers, and partners, in close coordination with DevRel.

• Plan and host quarterly executive receptions for key customers in partnership with Sales and Customer Success, focused on relationship depth, expansion, and advocacy.

• Lead PhoenixAI's presence at major industry conferences and partner events (e.g., AWS re:Invent) — sponsorship selection, booth, speaking opportunities, and on-site execution.

• Leverage the open-source data ecosystem — community members, other project communities, local meetup organizers — to source speakers, co-hosts, and venues for our events.

• Define the specific objective for each event before it happens — e.g., lead generation, pipeline influence, brand awareness, or customer engagement — and design the event and its metrics around that goal.

• Handle venue selection, sponsorship arrangements, vendor relationships, catering, booth setup, signage, promotional items, shipping, and travel logistics.

• Develop event schedules and keep colleagues, speakers, partners, and vendors aligned and on track.

• Produce landing pages, invites, social content, email outreach, and other materials to promote events.

• Work with speakers on presentations, demos, and run-of-show planning.

• Bring in internal technical resources — such as Product Management, Solutions Architects, and Engineering — to support event content and demos where needed.

• Partner with Sales ahead of each event to define target accounts, meeting objectives, and follow-up plans.

• Make sure leads gathered at events are logged accurately and passed along to Sales without delay.

• Capture and repurpose event content — recordings, photos, speaker decks — with the content and social teams.

• Coordinate with the team that owns webinars to align calendars and cross-promote where in-person and virtual programs overlap.

• Track and report on performance against the stated goal for each event (MQLs/SQLs generated, pipeline influence, awareness metrics, community growth, customer engagement, or similar).

• Keep an up-to-date calendar of upcoming conferences, sponsorship options, and community gatherings.

Qualifications

• 5+ years of field or event marketing experience at a fast-growing tech startup, ideally in the data, infrastructure, or SaaS space.

• Proven experience organizing events for an open-source or developer community — running meetups, community days, contributor gatherings, or community tracks at conferences. This is required.

• An existing network in the open-source data ecosystem (e.g., StarRocks, Apache projects, Linux Foundation events, or the broader data engineering community) that you can draw on for speakers, co-hosts, and venues is strongly preferred.

• Track record of running events end-to-end in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment, from large conference sponsorships to small executive hospitality events.

• Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally with internal technical stakeholders such as Solutions Architects, Product Managers, and DevRel.

• Strong vendor and budget management skills.

• Familiarity with event and community tooling (e.g., Luma, Bevy, Splash) and marketing automation / CRM systems (e.g., HubSpot, Salesforce).

• Comfortable engaging with technical speakers, partners, prospective customers, sales, and executive leadership.

• Willingness to travel for events and work evenings/weekends as needed around event schedules.

• Must currently be based in the San Francisco Bay Area.

• Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

When applying, please include 2–3 community or field events you have organized and your role in each.

The base salary for this role is projected at $150,000 - $200,000, plus eligibility for PhoenixAI's bonus and equity programs. Individual compensation will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location. We also provide a comprehensive benefits package featuring premium medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan. Employees enjoy at least 16 days of PTO, parental leave, health savings options, and access to our employee assistance program.

About the role

PhoenixAI is looking for a hands-on, data-driven Performance Marketing Manager to own our paid media programs end to end. You will take ownership of an active, multi-channel paid program and be responsible for auditing, restructuring, and scaling it: planning and running campaigns across search, social, programmatic, and account-based advertising, testing and iterating continuously, and making sure every dollar we spend can be traced to pipeline.

You will work closely with our GTM Systems team, which owns Salesforce and the GTM data stack, to build closed-loop attribution from ad spend to opportunities, and with product marketing, content, and design on messaging, creative, and landing pages. This is a builder role for someone who thrives on experimentation, moves fast, and wants to define how paid acquisition works at an early-stage company selling to enterprise data and AI teams.

What you'll do

As Performance Marketing Manager, you will own the strategy, execution, and measurement of PhoenixAI's paid media programs, driving qualified pipeline for our agentic AI database platform.

• Own and optimize our existing paid media programs across Google Search, LinkedIn, retargeting and programmatic display, account-based advertising (e.g., Demandbase), software review sites, content syndication, and sponsored placements in developer and data-engineering communities and newsletters.

• Run a continuous test-and-learn program across audiences, keywords, creative, offers, landing pages, and bidding strategies; optimize on a weekly cadence, document what works and what doesn't, and turn findings into repeatable playbooks.

• Research and evaluate new channels and ad formats, launch pilots with clear success criteria, and scale or cut them based on results.

• Define and enforce tracking standards (UTM conventions, conversion events, offline conversion imports) so that paid performance is measured against SQLs and pipeline, not just clicks and form fills.

• Partner with GTM Systems, which owns Salesforce and the GTM data stack, to integrate ad platform data, build closed-loop attribution, and maintain reporting from spend to pipeline.

• Work with product marketing, content, and design on ad messaging, creative, and high-converting landing pages; own conversion rate optimization for paid traffic.

• Manage the paid media budget in partnership with Finance, including pacing, forecasting, and monthly reconciliation.

• Manage relationships with media agencies, ad platform representatives, and vendors.

• Report on spend, efficiency, and pipeline contribution to marketing and GTM leadership, with clear, data-backed recommendations.

Qualifications

• 4–8 years of hands-on paid media / performance marketing experience, ideally within B2B SaaS or technology companies with enterprise sales cycles.

• Deep, hands-on expertise in Google Ads and LinkedIn Campaign Manager; experience with programmatic and account-based advertising platforms (e.g., Demandbase, 6sense, StackAdapt) is a strong plus.

• Experience building closed-loop measurement: offline conversion tracking, Salesforce campaign attribution, and reporting on cost per SQL and cost per opportunity.

• Strong analytical skills, with fluency in GA4, ad platform analytics, and spreadsheets; SQL or experience with BI tools is a plus.

• Track record of designing structured experiments and translating results into decisions.

• Experience with landing page and conversion rate optimization.

• Excellent project management skills and comfort managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Experience working cross-functionally with GTM, product marketing, content, and design teams.

• Familiarity with developer or data-engineering audiences, or with the open-source data ecosystem, is a plus.

• Bachelor's degree, preferably in Marketing, Communications, or a related field.

The base salary for this role is projected at $180,000 - $220,000 annually, plus eligibility for PhoenixAI's bonus programs. About the role

We are seeking a Technical Product Marketing Manager to drive the technical content, developer evangelism, and sales enablement that bring PhoenixAI's Agentic Database to market. This is a hands-on, hybrid role at the intersection of product marketing and developer relations: you'll write about the product, speak about it to engineers and technical buyers, demo it live, and arm our sales team to sell it. The ideal candidate is an engineer at heart who can also write and speak — someone who has built with data systems and can translate that depth into content, talks, and enablement that resonate with technical audiences.

What you'll do

As our Technical Product Marketing Manager, you'll be a key contributor to PhoenixAI's go-to-market, working across four connected areas: content, evangelism, enablement, and launches. Your responsibilities include:

• Technical Content Creation: Research, write, and publish technical content — blog posts, tutorials, benchmarks, competitive comparisons, and solution briefs — that demonstrates product depth and drives awareness and adoption among engineers and technical buyers.

• Developer Evangelism & Speaking: Represent PhoenixAI and StarRocks to technical audiences — deliver webinars, speak at meetups and industry conferences, and present live product demos to prospects and at events.

• Demos & Sample Code: Build and maintain product demos, sample applications, and short-form video content that showcase the Agentic Database in realistic scenarios; keep them current as the product evolves.

• Community Engagement: Engage directly with users in the StarRocks community channels, answer technical questions, surface recurring themes, and help grow an active, well-informed developer community around the open-source project.

• Sales Enablement: Build and deliver technical enablement for Sales and Solutions — pitch decks, battlecards, demo scripts, and FAQs — plus regular training sessions, new-hire onboarding, and competitive briefings that keep the field sharp on product and market.

• Product Launches & Competitive Intelligence: Support product and feature launches with launch content, demos, and enablement; track competitors such as ClickHouse, Snowflake, and Trino and turn what you learn into differentiated messaging, comparisons, and objection handling.

• Messaging & Feedback Loop: Contribute to PhoenixAI's positioning and messaging across the open-source (StarRocks) and commercial offerings, and bring signals from the community, customers, and sales back to product and marketing to sharpen the narrative.

• Cross-Functional Partnership: Work closely with product management, engineering, sales, and marketing to keep content, demos, and enablement accurate, current, and grounded in real product capabilities.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or another STEM field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 2+ years of experience in software engineering, solutions engineering, developer relations, technical product marketing, or a related technical role — ideally at a B2B data infrastructure or AI startup.

• Hands-on software development experience; proficient in SQL and comfortable building and presenting live product demos.

• Strong technical foundation in databases, distributed systems, or lakehouse architectures; able to hold your own in technical conversations with engineers and technical buyers.

• Strong writer who can produce clear, accurate technical content — from blog posts to tutorials to battlecards — with coaching on positioning and voice.

• Confident presenter, comfortable delivering technical talks, webinars, and demos live and fielding questions from engineers.

• Curious, high-energy, and eager to learn; thrives in a fast-moving, low-process startup environment and enjoys working across teams.

Strong plus:

• Experience speaking at meetups, webinars, or industry conferences.

• Familiarity with StarRocks, ClickHouse, Trino, Snowflake, Databricks, or similar analytical data systems.

• Experience contributing to or building around an open-source project and its community.

• Video or short-form content production experience.

Reports to: CEO
Key partners: VP of Finance; HRO (U.S. HR outsourcing partner)
Location: Menlo Park, CA, in-office at least four days per week
Employment type: Full-time
Team: Leads the U.S.-based People Experience and Recruiting team

About the role

This is PhoenixAI's first full-time HR leader in the U.S. You will build the company's HQ HR infrastructure and lead the U.S. people function for a growing company with teams in the U.S. and APAC. Your job is to set one standard for how PhoenixAI levels, pays, develops, and grows its people across the U.S. and APAC, and to make two teams operate as one company. You are a builder who sets the strategy and is also eager to roll up your sleeves and do much of the work yourself.

What you’ll do

Build one global people framework

• Create the job-leveling framework and title taxonomy used across the U.S.

• Partner with HR counterparts in APAC to align job leveling and compensation bands, benefits philosophy, and performance review cadence, while respecting statutory requirements and market norms in each jurisdiction.

• Build compensation bands and a single equity philosophy with the VP of Finance, designing and benchmarking OTE/MBO structure, new hire grants, refresh and promotion grants, and the annual refresh cycle

• Establish the performance review cycle, expectations, and documentation standard.

• Define promotion criteria and run calibration.

• Design the onboarding and offboarding experience.

• Build manager training around what it means to be an effective manager at PhoenixAI.

Grow the U.S. recruiting function

• Manage the U.S.-based recruiting team, who owns the hiring process end to end.

• Strengthen and scale in-house recruiting processes, practices, and tools, and grow the recruiting team as hiring demands.

• Partner with the VP of Finance and hiring managers to translate the headcount plan into a hiring roadmap, including the GTM hires the company has sequenced behind pipeline growth.

• Set interview standards and keep offers inside the comp bands.

Own the HRO partnership and HR systems

• Serve as the primary owner of the HRO relationship, which manages U.S. payroll, benefits administration and advisory, leave administration, compliance filings, the handbook, and the employee help desk. You set policy and direction, hold them to service levels, and resolve escalations.

• Handle sensitive employee relations matters and final people decisions directly.

• Own Rippling as the HR system of record, with the HRO supporting configuration. Build the people reporting that the founders and VP of Finance rely on.

Unite the U.S. and APAC (China & Singapore) teams culture

• Build programs, rituals, and communication that connect APAC engineering with the U.S. GTM, product, and engineering teams.

• Build connective tissue and a shared culture between our U.S. and APAC teams — helping the two groups work well together across time zones, language, and different working norms, and creating shared rituals and communication practices.

Partner across leadership

• CEO: people strategy, org design, culture, and the leadership team.

• VP of Finance: people budget, headcount planning, compensation, benefits cost, and HRO fees.

• APAC HR Partner: aligning leveling, comp bands, benefits philosophy, and performance cadence across the U.S., China, and Singapore while respecting local law and market norms. Also co-owning cross-regional culture programs, sharing employee relations issues that span across regions, and keeping global people data consistent.

• Executive leadership: trusted advisor on team design, hiring plans, performance, and organizational decisions, bringing both counsel and candor to senior conversations.

• Managers: coaching, performance, and employee relations.

What success looks like

First 90 days

• Take ownership of the HRO relationship and Rippling, with a clear scope split.

• Audit current policies, compensation, and titles across the U.S. and APAC.

• Assess recruiting processes with the recruiting team and set priorities.

Within 6 months

• Leveling, title taxonomy, comp bands, and the equity philosophy are approved and in use.

• A harmonized onboarding experience is live.

• The first performance review cycle has run on the new standard.

Within 12 months

• Promotions and calibration run on shared criteria across the U.S. and APAC.

• The OTE/MBO and variable comp structure is in place.

• Managers have completed training.

• Recruiting is scaling with the hiring plan.

• Employees in the U.S. and APAC describe working at one company rather than two.

Qualifications

• You have 7+ years in HR with broad generalist scope, including at least one stint as the first or founding HR leader at a venture-backed high-growth tech company.

• You have built leveling frameworks, comp bands, equity guidelines, and performance systems from scratch.

• You have led HR across more than one country, ideally the U.S. and China/Singapore, and harmonized policy, considering local requirements.

• You have managed a PEO or HRO partner and know where to delegate and where to stay hands-on.

• You have experience working with external employment counsel and know California employment law well.

• You have experience with Rippling or a similar HRIS.

• You have a solid grounding in recruiting and have managed or scaled a recruiting function.

• You are analytical and comfortable building headcount models with Finance.

Bonus: Professional proficiency in written and spoken Mandarin Chinese.

Every PhoenixAI hire is held to the same operating bar: own the outcome, seek truth and build trust, move fast with judgment, work AI-first, and raise the bar without ego.

Compensation

The base salary range for this role in the San Francisco Bay Area is $175,000 to $215,000. The offer also includes equity and PhoenixAI's full benefits package. Where you land in the range depends on your experience, scope, and interview results.

PhoenixAI is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

As a Database Support Engineer, you'll be the ongoing technical point of contact for customers, ensuring they realize sustained value from PhoenixAI's Agentic Database, while flexibly supporting the sales team as presales needs arise. Your responsibilities include:

• Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with sales to align technical discussions with business goals, address objections, and close deals, while gathering customer insights to shape PhoenixAI’s Agentic Database roadmap with product and engineering teams.

• Technical Expertise:

•

• Hands-on experience of OLAP workloads, query optimization, and data modeling (e.g., star schema, snowflake schema)

• Proficiency in SQL.

• Deep understanding of distributed data processing system theory.

• Familiar with at least one of the public cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure)

• Ambition & Curiosity: A driven, inquisitive mindset—eager to learn PhoenixAI Agentic Database product’s intricacies, tackle tough challenges, and grow into the role, even if starting with less experience or specific skills.

• Communication Skills: Proven ability to distill complex technical concepts into clear, compelling narratives for diverse stakeholders, from engineers to C-level executives.

• Problem-Solving: Adept at troubleshooting technical challenges during PoCs and adapting solutions to meet unique customer needs.

• Sales & Customer Success Mindset: Experience supporting sales and post-sales teams in technical evaluations, with a track record of securing technical wins and driving revenue growth.

• Bonus Points:

•

• Knowledge of BI tools (e.g., Tableau, Looker)

• Experience with streaming processing systems (Kafka, Redpanda, etc.)
